text:
alex: Heads-up — two us-west inference shards OOMed during the 11:40 traffic spike. I uploaded a quick flamegraph and allocation trace: https://internal.redwood/snapshots/1954219876 (flame + malloc traces).

maya: which model/route was hit?

alex: batch-rerank-prod-v2 (kernel-selector v1.8.2 rolled last night). p50 latency fine but mem peaked ~+1.7GB on GPU and then OOM.

tzeng: I saw a perf regression after the kernel selector update — small kernels got routed to a slower kernel that touches extra temp buffers. My perf diff: p50 +14%, p95 +22%, avg ephemeral allocations +1.3GB.

liam: quick profiling summary from the trace: kv_cache.entries grew 3x from typical due to many long-prefix queries; batch size distribution shifted toward many small batches + a tail of very large single-request sequences (>= 5k tokens). That combination triggered large workspace allocations.

alex: immediate mitigation plan (can do now from console):
1) enable canary fallback to q4_0-distil for 20% of traffic on rerank route (lower mem).
2) apply circuit breaker: per-customer concurrency cap 4, global per-shard concurrent_requests 16.
3) request shaping: enforce max_input_tokens 1024 for rerank requests and reject above with 429+retry-after.
4) kv_cache: set soft_limit=70% and ttl=5m to prune long-tail prefixes.
5) reduce max_batch_tokens from 4096 -> 1024 to avoid huge workspace allocations.

maya: can we flip these without a code rollback?

alex: yes — all are runtime config toggles except kernel-selector change. Rolling kernel-selector is last resort.

tzeng: attach quick breaker config snippet I used in the canary run earlier today:
```json
{
  "route": "batch-rerank-prod-v2",
  "circuit_breaker": {
    "per_customer_concurrency": 4,
    "per_shard_concurrency": 16,
    "reject_response": {"code": 429, "body": "rate_limited - retry after"}
  },
  "fallback": {"pct": 20, "model": "q4_0-distil"}
}
```

liam: commands for quick telemetry if you need numbers: 
- GPU mem sampling: ssh node && sudo nvidia-smi --query-gpu=memory.used --format=csv -l 1 -f /tmp/gpu-mem.csv &
- runtime allocator stats: curl -s http://localhost:9201/allocator/stats | jq '.'.
- kv cache stats: curl -s http://localhost:9201/kvstats | jq '.hot_prefixes | length, .memory_bytes'

alex: did a canary enable for fallback -> jr_server_bot should have applied the change.
jr_server_bot: change-applier: applied config set "batch-rerank-prod-v2.fallback.pct=20" by alex at 2026-03-18T11:55:12Z :white_check_mark:

ops-bot: routing-update: enabled canary fallback q4_0-distil on 20% of traffic (us-west only).

maya: nice. after that we still need to decide: revert kernel-selector commit or tune kernel selection policy?

alex: propose tune first: make kernel selector prefer low-temp-buffer variant when input_length > 1024 OR when batch_tokens > 2048. That avoids the buffer-heavy kernel for large sequences. If we still get OOMs after tuning + breakers, rollback the selector commit.

tzeng: agree. Also, enable buffer reuse heuristics: buffer_reuse.enabled=true but with reuse_threshold=32KB to avoid tiny-chunk fragmentation. That saved ~400MB in past runs.

liam: reminder: buffer_reuse sometimes increases allocation lifespan leading to higher peak if reuse causes retained fragments. Suggested sequence: enable reuse + kv eviction + stricter breakers; monitor 30m. If peak still > baseline -> rollback kernel selector.

alex: monitoring checklist I pushed to the incident channel:
- watch allocator/stats for "peak_reused" and "peak_allocated"
- watch kvstats.memory_bytes and eviction_rate
- p50/p95 latency for rerank route
- OOM counts from nodes via /metrics (oom_count)

maya: after 30m we'll convene for rollback decision. I can own rollback if needed.

alex: logging what we changed (for postmortem):
- fallback q4_0-distil 20% (canary)
- request_shaper max_input_tokens 1024
- circuit breaker per_customer 4 / per_shard 16
- kv_cache soft_limit 70% / ttl 5m
- max_batch_tokens 1024
- buffer_reuse.enabled=true reuse_threshold=32KB (canary)

liam: quick heads-up: add a short eval to ensure q4_0 rerank quality is acceptable on canary traffic. I'll set up a perf check to surface regression >1.5% quality drop.

alex: thanks all. tagging @ops for infra awareness. We'll reconvene in 30m or earlier if OOMs stop/continue. :hourglass_flowing_sand:

ops-bot: note: incident ticket INC-2026-241 opened and linked to this thread.

maya: closing loop — will post outcome in 30m. :white_check_mark:
